title: Trim a sheet on a two-speed sailboat winch: grind in fast gear, reverse into slow gear to full trim, stow the handle
instruction: Trim the sheet in on the winch until the red mark on the sheet reaches the drum's edge, then put the winch handle back in its holder.
context: Grinding a sheet in on a winch is the job a short clip of a sailboat under way shows; US boating is broad: 11,674,073 recreational vessels were registered in 2024 (US Coast Guard) and "85M Americans Go Boating Each Year" (NMMA, citing a 2018 Coast Guard survey). On a two-speed winch the handle's direction picks the gear; Harken's Rewind winch manual: "As the load increases, activate second speed by turning the handle in the opposite direction." The difficulty is in the hands: precise control of force and position under a rising load, with the gear changed by reversing the crank when first gear gets too hard, against pawls that allow no backing off; then a locking handle that takes two hands to remove: one holds its lock lever turned while the other lifts it out. Plain crank turning has neither the rising load nor the gear change. The robot grinds; a hanging weight tails the sheet, as a second crew member would.
setup: Millimetres; x away from the robot, y to its left, z up from the bench. 18 mm plywood deck board 480 x 740 centred at (380, 230), clamped. Harken Performa 20.2PTP two-speed plain-top winch bolted with its axis at (400, 100); first gear clockwise seen from above (the maker's convention as summarised; unverified). Lewmar 250 mm (10 in) grey alloy locking winch handle, part 29141111 (modelled 254 long, 600 g), grip and lock lever drawn red (the listings do not state colours), standing in its holder (an open socket on a post, no lock, top 100 above the deck board) at (250, 500), its arm 52 deg right of straight ahead. The lock lever lies on the hub's top 72 deg anticlockwise from the arm, its tab 40 from the axis; turned anticlockwise 20 deg (of 30) against its 2-5 N spring it frees the lock (lever geometry and spring are estimates). A 10 mm double-braid sheet runs along x = 358.5: from springs below the bench's -y edge over an edge roller at y = -640, through a fairlead on the deck board's edge at y = -120, three clockwise turns on the drum, then the tail along +y over an edge roller at y = +640 to a 1.0 kg weight hanging 120 below the bench top. Springs: A 200 N/m with 30 N preload; B 934 N/m on a slack link taking up after 150 mm; sheet load 30 N at the start, 60 N at 150 mm, 351 N at full trim. A red mark on the sheet 406.9 from the drum's edge; a stopper ball meets the fairlead's rubber snubber at full trim. A 6 in horn cleat on a vertical board at (569, 480), unused.
scoring: 1.0: the red mark within 5 mm of the drum's edge (or past it), reached within 4 handle turns (both directions, counted while the sheet moves; first gear then second took 2.99 in the demo, second alone 4.83), with the handle out of the winch and standing in its holder, both hands at least 30 mm from the handle, and the handle, knob, lock lever and winch spindle each under 10 mm/s, held 1 s. 0.75: the mark within 5 mm without that full finish (more than 4 turns, not in its holder, a hand within 30 mm, a part moving, or not yet held 1 s). 0.5: 5 to 30 mm short with that finish (turns not counted); 0.25: 30 to 80 mm short with it; an untidy finish steps 0.5 and 0.25 down one rung. 0 otherwise, and for the whole trial if the handle is dropped (falling at 1 m/s or more with no gripper on it, not in the winch or holder: it can go overboard or land on a foot). Void (0) if the parts' or arms' state can't be read, a write fails, the simulation goes non-finite, or a new trial's parts aren't within 5 mm of their start. Read at the trial's end. In the winch: from when the spigot is 6 mm into the socket (axis within 2 mm of the socket's, tilt within 8 deg) until lifted 23 mm with the lock free; in the holder: from seating (axis within 4 mm, tilt within 8 deg, within 4 mm of seated) until lifted 23 mm. The lock frees once its lever is turned 20 deg and latches again only below 10 deg (fully in: locked; part way: caught there). Turns: the handle's turns about the winch's axis while they drive the drum (both directions take the sheet in), summed; the 3 deg of free play after each reversal does not count, nor does jiggling of under 0.5 deg. By hand: count the knob's revolutions on the video while the mark moves toward the drum. First gear is there to bring the sheet in quickly while the load is light; the turn count stands in for that without timing the arm, so second gear alone, which trims fully but slowly, loses one step (0.75), not the trim. Gripper on it: pads under 60 mm apart with a point between them within 5 mm of the handle. Real trial: a ruler on the sheet from the mark to the drum's edge, the knob's turns counted on the video, a photo of the handle in its holder, the video for hands and drops.
reset_notes: About 3 minutes (an estimate, not timed). Take the turns off the drum and let the springs draw the sheet back until the mark is 406.9 from the drum's edge; put three clockwise turns back on; hang the tail weight 120 below the bench top; stand the handle in its holder, arm as at the start. Before a session check the rig with a luggage scale on the sheet at the fairlead: 30 N, 60 N and 351 N with the mark 406.9, 256.9 and 0 from the drum's edge.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX at real size. The socket's fit is a joint, not contact: within 2 mm and 8 deg of the axis the spigot is held across and slides along it; a latch (a stiff spring on that slide) stops it unless the lever is held turned, going in as well as out (modelled, not sourced). Gears are a per-step coupling (1:1 or 1:2.76 by the handle's direction; never back), felt at the handle as a brake. Sheet, turns, tail and weight are drawn; the load is a spring law. Untested on a real winch.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1 trial, all 6,000 steps); demo: 1.0 on 3 of 3 trials (full trim after 2.99 turns; handle out with both hands, stowed). Negatives: nothing 0; first gear only 0; second gear only 0.75; left in 0.75; pulled without the lever 0.75; lever let go before the lift 0.75; dropped 0.
